name: 48983-randomdecode-gemma4moe26b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1), sm90.
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1, no expert parallelism; one engine built in-process through guidellm's vllm_python backend, so there is no HTTP server on this path.
architecture: Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration, a vision-language checkpoint driven text-only here. ~18.83 GB over two safetensors shards, ungated and apache-2.0.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams = 1, warmup 10%, cooldown 10%, bounded at 40 requests with a 1800 s safety cap, seed static 48983. Budget 5-10 minutes of traffic plus model load.
workload: single-turn plain text synthesised by guidellm: 1024 prompt tokens and 1024 output tokens, both pinned min == max so no length can drift. `request_format: plain`, no chat template and no sampling parameters; the backend sets ignore_eos, so the generation length is exact.
purpose: A long-form writing assistant on one GPU, serving a single user 1024-token prompts and 1024-token replies.
launch:
# Launch config for 48983-randomdecode-gemma4moe26b-1gpu. The interpreter and the hardware seal are
# in `env.yaml`. Nothing here is tuned: every line is either the declared deployment shape or the
# engine's own default at this commit, written out so it cannot drift.

model: nvidia/Gemma-4-26B-A4B-NVFP4

tensor-parallel-size: 1
pipeline-parallel-size: 1
enable-expert-parallel: false

# Every request is 1024 prompt tokens plus exactly 1024 generated, so 4096 clears it with room.
max-model-len: 4096

trust-remote-code: true

# BOTH LOAD-BEARING; do not drop either as "the default". This item builds the engine in-process
# through AsyncLLM, whose usage context is in neither per-context default dict, so both arguments
# would otherwise fall through to the SchedulerConfig floors of 2048 and 128.
max-num-batched-tokens: 8192
max-num-seqs: 1024

gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90
enable-prefix-caching: true

# `enforce-eager` is deliberately unset: CUDA graph capture and `torch.compile` stay on, which is
# the ordinary serving condition.
